```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Gomeni 2019 presents a framework for choosing the dose and the in vitro
release of an extended-release product that maximise its benefit-risk ratio:
a convolution-based in vitro/in vivo correlation (IVIVC) links the in vitro
dissolution of a formulation to its plasma concentrations, and an
exposure-response model links those concentrations to a clinical score. The
case study is methylphenidate (MPH) from Ritalin LA, a bimodal
extended-release capsule. Two models from the paper are packaged:

* `Gomeni_2019_methylphenidate_ir` -- the one-compartment model of Ritalin IR
  (step 1 of the analysis, Table S1), whose elimination rate and volume are
  the disposition of the IVIVC.
* `Gomeni_2019_methylphenidate_ivivc` -- the convolution IVIVC (steps 2 and 3,
  Tables S2 and S3, final Scenario 2 with a common relative bioavailability).

```{r model-meta}
mod_ir <- readModelDb("Gomeni_2019_methylphenidate_ir")
mod_ivivc <- readModelDb("Gomeni_2019_methylphenidate_ivivc")

# Both models were fitted to mean data and declare no random effects, so a
# solve gives the typical profile. rxode2 warns on every multi-subject solve
# without omega; muffle that one warning only.
solve_typical <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

* IR model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_ir)$description`
* IVIVC model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_ivivc)$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_ivivc)$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12378>

The exposure-response part of the paper (Eqs. 13-15: an indirect-response
placebo model, an Emax drug effect and a time-dependent EC50 for tolerance,
driving the SKAMP score) is not packaged. The paper runs it with "the
parameter values previously estimated" in Gomeni et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther
2017;102:951-960 (doi:10.1002/cpt.684), and does not print any of them.

# Population

The data are the published mean profiles of Wang et al. (Biopharm Drug Dispos
2004;25:91-98), digitised by the authors: a four-period, four-treatment,
single-dose randomised crossover in healthy volunteers after at least a
10-hour fast. 17 subjects were enrolled and 16 were kept in the PK analysis.
The treatments were three Ritalin LA 40 mg capsule formulations chosen for
slow, medium and fast in vitro dissolution, and Ritalin IR (two 20 mg tablets
4 h apart) as the reference. Age, weight and sex are not reported in Gomeni
2019. Because only mean data were fitted, neither model has between-subject
variability; both have an additive residual error. The same information is
available programmatically via `rxode2::rxode(mod_ivivc)$population`.

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IR structure | 1 compartment, first-order absorption with lag, first-order elimination | Results, Step 1 |
| `lka` (IR) | ka = 2.39 1/h | Table S1 |
| `ltlag` (IR) | Lag = 0.63 h | Table S1 |
| `lkel` (IR and IVIVC) | kel = 0.254 1/h | Control stream `KEL=0.254`; Table S1 prints 0.25 |
| `lvc` (IR and IVIVC) | V = 1.2 kL = 1200 L | Table S1 `V = 1.20`; control stream `S1=1.2` with dose in mg and concentrations in ng/mL |
| `addSd` (IR) | 0.60 ng/mL | Table S1 `err_add` |
| In vitro release | double Weibull, unreleased fraction `ff*exp(-(t/td)^ss) + (1-ff)*exp(-(t/td1)^ss1)` | Eq. 9; control stream `$PK` |
| `lra_<form>` | ra = 1/td: slow 1/0.186, medium 1/0.159, fast 1/0.17 1/h | Control stream `TD`; Table S2 td 0.19 / 0.16 / 0.17 h |
| `lgam1_<form>` | ss: 1.7 / 6.55 / 1.79 | Control stream `SS`; Table S2 |
| `lra2_<form>` | ra2 = 1/td1: 1/9.91, 1/7.55, 1/5.42 1/h | Control stream `TD1`; Table S2 |
| `lgam2_<form>` | ss1: 3.59 / 2.63 / 1.75 | Control stream `SS1`; Table S2 |
| `logitfrel_<form>` | ff: 0.5 / 0.502 / 0.471 | Control stream `FF`; Table S2 0.50 / 0.50 / 0.47 |
| IVIVC time scaling | rvivo(t) = a1 + a2 rvitro(tt), tt = b1 + b2 t^b3 | Eq. 3 / Eq. 10; control stream `$DES` |
| `ivivc_int`, `ivivc_slope`, `ivivc_tshift` | a1 = 0, a2 = 1, b1 = 0, all fixed | Table S3 Scenario 2 |
| `livivc_tscale` | b2 = 0.19 | Table S3 Scenario 2 |
| `livivc_tshape` | b3 = 2.24 | Table S3 Scenario 2 |
| `lfdepot` | F = 0.94 | Table S3 Scenario 2 |
| `addSd` (IVIVC) | 1.13 ng/mL | Table S3 Scenario 2 `err_add` |
| Input rate | central difference, step 0.01 h, times floored at 0, release clamped to [0, 1] | Eq. 11; control stream `DELT=0.01` and `$DES` |
| Disposition ODE | dA/dt = F Dose f(t) - kel A; Cp = A/V | Eq. 12; control stream `DADT(1)` |

# Ritalin IR (Figure S1)

Ritalin IR was given as two 20 mg tablets 4 h apart.

```{r ir-sim}
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), 3, 7, 12)))
ev_ir <- rxode2::et(amt = 20, time = c(0, 4), cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(grid, cmt = "central")
sim_ir <- as.data.frame(solve_typical(mod_ir, ev_ir))
```

```{r ir-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure S1 (linear panel) of Gomeni 2019: typical Ritalin IR profile after two 20 mg tablets 4 h apart."}
ggplot(sim_ir, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "MPH concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Values the maintainers read off the model curve of Figure S1 are compared
with the packaged model at the two peaks, the trough and 24 h.

```{r ir-check}
ir_peak1 <- sim_ir |> filter(time <= 4) |> slice_max(Cc, n = 1)
ir_trough <- sim_ir |> filter(time > 3, time <= 5) |> slice_min(Cc, n = 1)
ir_peak2 <- sim_ir |> filter(time > 4) |> slice_max(Cc, n = 1)
ir_24 <- sim_ir |> filter(time == 24)
ir_cmp <- data.frame(
  feature = c("First peak", "Trough", "Second peak", "24 h"),
  figure_S1 = c(12.4, 7.0, 18.0, 0.19),
  simulated = c(ir_peak1$Cc, ir_trough$Cc, ir_peak2$Cc, ir_24$Cc),
  sim_time_h = c(ir_peak1$time, ir_trough$time, ir_peak2$time, 24)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - figure_S1) / figure_S1)
ir_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Feature" = feature, "Figure S1 (ng/mL)" = figure_S1,
    "Simulated (ng/mL)" = simulated, "Simulated time (h)" = sim_time_h,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# Deterministic typical-value solve against values read off a figure: the
# reading error is about 0.3 ng/mL, so 15% is the envelope for the peaks and
# trough. The 24 h value is near the axis floor and is checked only for order.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ir_cmp$pct_diff[1:3]) < 15),
  ir_24$Cc > 0.1, ir_24$Cc < 0.4
)
```

# In vitro dissolution (Figure 4)

```{r forms}
forms <- data.frame(
  formulation = factor(c("Slow", "Medium", "Fast"), levels = c("Slow", "Medium", "Fast")),
  FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM = c(0L, 1L, 0L),
  FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST = c(0L, 0L, 1L)
)
ini_ivivc <- rxode2::rxode(mod_ivivc)$theta
weibull_set <- function(form) {
  sfx <- tolower(form)
  list(
    ra = exp(ini_ivivc[[paste0("lra_", sfx)]]),
    gam1 = exp(ini_ivivc[[paste0("lgam1_", sfx)]]),
    ra2 = exp(ini_ivivc[[paste0("lra2_", sfx)]]),
    gam2 = exp(ini_ivivc[[paste0("lgam2_", sfx)]]),
    frel = plogis(ini_ivivc[[paste0("logitfrel_", sfx)]])
  )
}
unreleased <- function(t, p) {
  p$frel * exp(-(p$ra * t)^p$gam1) + (1 - p$frel) * exp(-(p$ra2 * t)^p$gam2)
}
b2 <- exp(ini_ivivc[["livivc_tscale"]])
b3 <- exp(ini_ivivc[["livivc_tshape"]])
diss <- tidyr::expand_grid(formulation = forms$formulation, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    in_vitro = 100 * (1 - unreleased(time, weibull_set(as.character(formulation)))),
    in_vivo = 100 * (1 - unreleased(b2 * time^b3, weibull_set(as.character(formulation))))
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r diss-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "Replicates the model curves of Figure 4 of Gomeni 2019 (in vitro, solid) and adds the time-scaled in vivo release of the IVIVC (dashed)."}
diss |>
  pivot_longer(c(in_vitro, in_vivo), names_to = "process", values_to = "pct") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, pct, linetype = process)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~formulation) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Released (% of dose)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The time scaling `tt = 0.19 t^2.24` makes in vivo time run slower than the
dissolution test before about 2.1 h (where `tt = t`) and faster after it, so
the first in vitro release phase (`td` about 0.17 h) is spread over the first
hour in vivo, and the second phase is compressed into roughly 3-8 h.

# Convolution IVIVC (Figure 5 and Table 1)

```{r ivivc-sim}
grid48 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.05), 3, 7, 12)))
ev_ivivc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(forms)), function(i) {
  ev <- as.data.frame(rxode2::et(amt = 40, cmt = "depot") |> rxode2::et(grid48, cmt = "central"))
  ev$id <- i
  ev$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM <- forms$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM[i]
  ev$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST <- forms$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST[i]
  ev
}))
sim_ivivc <- as.data.frame(solve_typical(mod_ivivc, ev_ivivc, keep = c("FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM", "FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST"))) |>
  mutate(formulation = forms$formulation[id])
```

```{r fig5, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "Replicates the model-predicted curves of Figure 5 of Gomeni 2019: typical MPH concentrations after a single 40 mg dose of each Ritalin LA formulation."}
sim_ivivc |>
  filter(time <= 24) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~formulation) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "MPH concentration (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The maintainers read the slow-formulation model curve of Figure 5 at its
first peak, its trough and its second peak.

```{r fig5-check}
slow <- sim_ivivc |> filter(formulation == "Slow")
fig5_cmp <- data.frame(
  time = c(1.5, 4, 7, 12),
  figure_5 = c(13.6, 8.0, 14.4, 3.8)
) |>
  left_join(slow |> select(time, Cc), by = "time") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Cc - figure_5) / figure_5)
fig5_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Figure 5 (ng/mL)" = figure_5, "Simulated (ng/mL)" = Cc, "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# Deterministic solve against a figure reading (about 0.3 ng/mL).
stopifnot(all(abs(fig5_cmp$pct_diff) < 10))
```

## PKNCA

Table 1 reports Cmax, AUC to infinity and three partial AUCs (0-3, 3-7 and
7-12 h, the FDA metrics for Ritalin LA bioequivalence) for the observed and
the convolution-predicted profiles. The predicted columns are the model's own
output and are the reference here.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim_ivivc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, formulation) |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(formulation))
dose <- conc |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(time = 0, amt = 40)
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 0, 3, 7), end = c(Inf, 3, 7, 12),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
  aucinf.obs = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "auclast")) |>
  mutate(interval = ifelse(is.infinite(end), "0-inf", paste0(start, "-", end))) |>
  select(treatment, interval, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

ref_nca <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    treatment = c("Slow", "Medium", "Fast"), interval = "0-inf",
    PPTESTCD = "cmax", PPORRES = c(14.12, 14.6, 14.7)
  ),
  data.frame(
    treatment = c("Slow", "Medium", "Fast"), interval = "0-inf",
    PPTESTCD = "aucinf.obs", PPORRES = c(122.94, 123.77, 123.47)
  ),
  data.frame(
    treatment = rep(c("Slow", "Medium", "Fast"), each = 3),
    interval = rep(c("0-3", "3-7", "7-12"), 3),
    PPTESTCD = "auclast",
    PPORRES = c(25.49, 40.98, 27.43, 26.95, 47.2, 23.9, 26.41, 53.39, 31.22)
  )
)

cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_nca, ref_nca,
  by = c("treatment", "interval"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs Table 1 (convolution-predicted values) of Gomeni 2019, 40 mg single dose. 'AUClast' rows are the partial AUCs over the stated interval.")
```

```{r pknca-check}
pct <- sim_nca |>
  inner_join(ref_nca, by = c("treatment", "interval", "PPTESTCD"), suffix = c("_sim", "_ref")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES_sim - PPORRES_ref) / PPORRES_ref)
pct_main <- pct |> filter(!(interval == "7-12" & treatment %in% c("Slow", "Medium")))
pct_late <- pct |> filter(interval == "7-12", treatment %in% c("Slow", "Medium"))
# Typical-value solve of a fixed model against the authors' predictions from
# the same model: Cmax, AUCinf, pAUC0-3, pAUC3-7 and the fast pAUC7-12 agree
# within 5%. The slow and medium pAUC7-12 of Table 1 cannot be produced by the
# Figure 5 curves (see Assumptions and deviations), so they are checked to
# stay above Table 1, not to match it.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(pct_main$pct_diff) < 5),
  all(pct_late$pct_diff > 25)
)
```

All Cmax, AUC0-inf, pAUC0-3 and pAUC3-7 values agree with the paper's
predictions within 4%. The fast-formulation pAUC7-12 agrees within 3%. The
slow and medium pAUC7-12 rows are flagged: the packaged model gives about 40
and 35 ng*h/mL where Table 1 prints 27.43 and 23.90 (and 25.66 and 25.32 for
the observed data). Those printed values are not consistent with the paper's
own Figure 5. On the slow panel, both the model curve and the observed means
fall from about 14 ng/mL at 7 h to about 4 ng/mL at 12 h. A single
exponential decline between those two points has an area of
(14 - 4) / (log(14 / 4) / 5) = 40 ng*h/mL, and the Figure 5 curves fall more
slowly than that just after 7 h, not faster. The model was not adjusted.

# Dose range (Figure 6a, PK panels)

Figure 6a simulates Ritalin LA at the recommended doses of 10, 20 and 40 mg.
The model is linear, so exposure scales with dose.

```{r dose-range, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "PK panels of Figure 6a of Gomeni 2019: typical MPH concentrations after 10, 20 and 40 mg of each Ritalin LA formulation."}
ev_dose <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(forms)), function(i) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c(10, 20, 40), function(d) {
    ev <- as.data.frame(rxode2::et(amt = d, cmt = "depot") |> rxode2::et(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), cmt = "central"))
    ev$id <- (i - 1) * 3 + match(d, c(10, 20, 40))
    ev$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM <- forms$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_MEDIUM[i]
    ev$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST <- forms$FORM_METHYLPHENIDATE_FAST[i]
    ev
  }))
}))
sim_dose <- as.data.frame(solve_typical(mod_ivivc, ev_dose)) |>
  mutate(
    formulation = forms$formulation[(id - 1) %/% 3 + 1],
    dose = factor(c(10, 20, 40)[(id - 1) %% 3 + 1])
  )
ggplot(sim_dose, aes(time, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~formulation) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "MPH concentration (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)") +
  theme_bw()
cmax_dose <- sim_dose |>
  group_by(formulation, dose) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
cmax_dose |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = dose, values_from = cmax) |>
  dplyr::rename("Formulation" = formulation, "Cmax 10 mg" = `10`, "Cmax 20 mg" = `20`, "Cmax 40 mg" = `40`) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# Linear disposition and a dose-proportional input: Cmax is proportional to
# dose up to the ODE solver tolerance.
stopifnot(all(abs(cmax_dose |>
  group_by(formulation) |>
  summarise(r = max(cmax) / min(cmax) / 4 - 1) |>
  pull(r)) < 1e-3))
```

The Discussion quotes Cmax values of 3.96, 7.92 and 15.85 ng/mL at 10, 20 and
40 mg for the reference formulation, proportional to dose as here. The
paper's 40 mg value is 5-9% above the packaged model's Cmax for any of the
three formulations and the Figure 6a profile (about 16 ng/mL at both peaks,
trough about 11 ng/mL) does not match any of the three Figure 5 curves; the
paper does not say which formulation or which input model the "Ref" curves
of Figure 6 use, so they are not reproduced exactly.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Control-stream values used for the dissolution sets and kel.** Table S2
  prints td to two decimals (0.19, 0.16, 0.17 h) and ff as 0.50, 0.50, 0.47;
  Table S1 prints kel as 0.25 1/h. The authors' NONMEM control stream, which
  produced the IVIVC estimates, carries TD = 0.186, 0.159, 0.17 h, FF = 0.5,
  0.502, 0.471 and KEL = 0.254 1/h, and those values are used. The IR model
  uses the same kel = 0.254 1/h.
* **Volume units.** Table S1 prints V = 1.20 with unit "L". With the dose in
  mg and concentrations in ng/mL (the control stream scales `S1 = 1.2`), V is
  1.2 kL, i.e. 1200 L; the model carries `vc` in L and converts mg/L to ng/mL.
* **Placement of the linear IVIVC factors.** Eq. 3 applies a1 and a2 to the
  released fraction, `rvivo = a1 + a2 * rvitro(tt)`. The control stream
  applies them to the unreleased fraction (`FA = A1 + A2*VV`) and clamps the
  result to [0, 1]. The model follows the code. With a1 = 0 and a2 = 1, as
  fitted, the two forms are identical.
* **Numerical input rate.** The in vivo input rate is the central difference
  of the scaled release with the control stream's step of 0.01 h, not its
  analytical derivative. The step matters most for the medium formulation,
  whose first release phase is very steep (ss = 6.55), so its first peak is
  sensitive to the output grid.
* **Single dose.** The input is computed from the most recent dose and the
  time since it (`podo()` and `tad0()`), as in the authors' code, which only
  had single doses. It is exact for a single dose and for once-daily dosing
  once the previous dose has been fully released (about 12 h in vivo for all
  three formulations); overlapping doses are not superposed.
* **Final model.** Table S3 reports two scenarios. Scenario 2 (one F for all
  formulations; B2 0.19, B3 2.24, F 0.94, err_add 1.13; OFV 61.402) was
  preferred by the likelihood-ratio test and is packaged. Scenario 1 (F_slow
  0.96, F_medium 0.92, F_fast 0.95; B2 0.20, B3 2.24, err_add 1.12; OFV
  60.974) is not.
* **No variability.** Both fits used mean data; the IVIVC control stream
  carries `$OMEGA 0 FIX`. The models are typical-value models with additive
  residual error. The 80/90/95% prediction intervals of Figure 5 are not
  reproduced; their source is not described.
* **Table 1 partial AUCs.** The slow and medium pAUC7-12 values of Table 1
  (observed and predicted) are inconsistent with Figure 5, as shown above.
  They are reported as printed and not used to adjust the model.
* **SKAMP exposure-response.** Not packaged; its parameter values are only in
  Gomeni 2017 (Clin Pharmacol Ther 102:951) and are not printed in this paper.
* **Errata.** No erratum to Gomeni 2019 was found (Europe PMC, checked
  2026-11-25).
